_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel's down a second straight week — $6.199 for 10/5, off 18 cents — so reprice your fuel surcharge off the current index and stay fair with shippers, but hold your base linehaul; don't let fuel drag it down. Reefer's softening underneath as produce winds down (Pacific Northwest reefer already slipped), so don't chase it — but Yakima-to-East-Coast apples are still paying $12.6k+ a load, so push those.

_sourcing.status: SIXTEENTH straight cycle with WebFetch/curl egress blocked (WebFetch www.eia.gov and www.dat.com = getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND; curl eia.gov = CONNECT tunnel 403). WebSearch only (one USDA FVWTRK PDF on s3.amazonaws.com was fetchable but unreadable - compressed/image content, no table text extracted). asOf advanced 2026-09-28 -> 2026-10-05 on the strength of the EIA diesel week-ending 10/5 print ONLY; every other field is still on its prior reading date (see per-field notes). EIA week of 10/12 NOT found.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE (medium-high confidence, secondary sources). $6.199/gal for EIA week ending 2026-10-05, down $0.183 from $6.382 (9/28) - second straight decline. Two independent hits: (1) a news item stating the EIA national average fell 'from $6.382 to $6.199' with Brent down 1.3% to $99.07 (undated snippet, but its starting point matches the confirmed 9/28 print and the arithmetic checks); (2) a secondary report of $6.20 for week ending Oct 5 (also regional: West Coast $7.23, Midwest $6.29, East Coast $5.95). No primary EIA read (egress blocked) and no major trade-press headline retrieved. Prior: $6.382 (9/28), $6.529 record (9/21). NOT USED: AAA retail $6.32 (non-EIA survey). Rejected as stale-year/regime artifacts: TheTrucker $5.351 item, CasterHQ $5.967 (week of 9/7, older week), all ~$3-4 diesel items. EIA week of 10/12 (published 10/13) NOT found - next cycle.
_sourcing.trend: DOWN, confirmed continuing: second straight EIA decline (9/28 -> 10/5, -18.3c). Diesel-driven. Caveat: all-in spot (NTI) and DAT van linehaul were still firm as of the last readings, so 'down' reflects fuel easing, not freight rates falling.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: CARRIED FORWARD, NOT re-verified this cycle (no newer NTI/DAT national read surfaced; FreightWaves search returned only early-Sept NTI $3.44). Prior note: $3.53/mi, FreightWaves SONAR NTI (dry van incl. fuel) 'climbed back to $3.53' per FreightWaves 'Truckload's mixed signals' (published ~10/4; reading ~10/2-3). Up from $3.42 (9/16). Cross-checks: FreightWaves 9/28 piece implied ~$3.45 (5.2% above $3.28); one other summary showed $3.55. Single clean source and the exact reading date is approximate (~10/3), so medium confidence; this is newer than asOf 9/28 by a few days.
_sourcing.modality: CARRIED FORWARD unchanged - no national DAT van/reefer/flatbed all-in for weeks ending 10/3 or 10/10 surfaced (latest retrievable national is still week 9/20-26 below). Only new reefer signal: DAT top-10 origin table, week ending 10/3, Pacific Northwest reefer $3.07/mi, -3.2% w/w (-$0.10), +46% y/y - regional, NOT a national reprice; DAT reefer load-to-truck ratio 21.65 (quarter-end push); 35-day forecast reefer linehaul ~$2.75. REEFER NOT YET CONFIRMED ROLLED OVER nationally - directional softening only; with diesel down 18c two weeks running, expect national reefer all-in to drop once DAT's lagged fuel surcharge catches up. No repricing, so commodity mappings (dry van->General Dry Freight 3.01; reefer->Frozen Seafood/Poultry+Fresh Produce 3.63; flatbed->Coiled Steel 3.60) remain in sync. Prior note: DAT all-in, week 9/20-26 (Overdrive 9/30 quoting DAT; TheTrucker 'Load posts down 1%'): Dry Van $3.01 (reported +5c; linehaul $2.17 held flat — fuel was the entire move), Reefer PROMOTED $3.59 -> $3.63 (+4c; linehaul $2.71 FELL — fuel more than accounted for the rise), Flatbed PROMOTED to $3.60 (+5c; linehaul $2.59 fell). FLAG: van $3.01 / +5c also matches the earlier AJOT 9/13-19 headline, so one of the two weeks may be mislabeled by sources; van held at $3.01 rather than guess. REEFER SOFTENING: first visible — reefer linehaul fell, and Truckstop/FTR broker-posted reefer rates 'slid as expected' (Overdrive 9/30). All-in still up only because of the fuel pass-through; with diesel now falling, expect reefer all-in to roll over next cycle. yoy fields unchanged (DAT linehaul yoy, older reading; search summaries were inconsistent on newer values, so not touched). LTL and Intermodal unchanged, no new data.
_sourcing.commodityRates: All carried forward unchanged, in sync with modality: General Dry Freight 3.01 (dry van), Frozen Seafood/Poultry and Fresh Produce 3.63 (reefer), Coiled Steel 3.60 (flatbed). NOTE: the file shows Coiled Steel 3.60, but the app's FALLBACK_MARKET_RATES still has 3.57 (only the live JSON overrides it). High-Value Electronics 2.60 carried forward, no data.
_sourcing.lanes: Yakima, WA -> Northeast (reefer) CARRIED FORWARD from USDA week ended 9/29 (a USDA FVWTRK report for Tue 10/6, issued 10/7, exists at barchart s3 20261007-fvwtrk.pdf but could not be text-extracted, so the 10/6 Boston/NY midpoints are unread - best next-cycle target; PNW reefer -3.2% w/w per DAT suggests further easing). Prior note, REFRESHED LIVE: USDA AMS refrigerated truck rates, week ended 2026-09-29, via IndexBox summary of agtransport.usda.gov: Boston midpoint $12,650, New York $12,600 (Miami $14,150 for reference). Down from prior week (Boston $13,650 -> $12,650; NY $12,950 -> $12,600) — first sign of Yakima easing. Range shown covers only the two Northeast lanes confirmed for 9/29; Baltimore/Philadelphia 9/29 midpoints not confirmed (Philadelphia $11,500 and Baltimore $11,700 are from 9/22). Atlanta -> Miami: CARRIED FORWARD, unchanged, 16 cycles — only generic broker/blog ranges ($2.20-3.00 reefer) surfaced, no clean dated absolute $/mi; NOT promoted. Memphis -> Atlanta: not searched, unchanged.
_sourcing.blurb: Rewritten around the second straight diesel decline ($6.199, 10/5): reprice surcharge off the index, hold base linehaul, reefer softening (PNW down), Yakima still strong at $12.6k+ (9/29 reading).
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: (1) Diesel $6.199 (10/5) rests on secondary sources, no primary EIA read; EIA week of 10/12 not found. (2) Only dieselPerGal/trend/blurb moved this cycle; spotAllIn, modality, commodityRates, lanes are older readings (9/20-26 DAT, ~10/3 NTI, 9/29 USDA) under a 10/5 asOf badge. (3) Van $3.01 duplicated across two DAT weeks in sources. (4) Atlanta->Miami needs a clean dated absolute $/mi. (5) Read the USDA 10/6 FVWTRK for Yakima; watch national reefer all-in roll over.

refreshBlockers: Egress re-tested first: WebFetch to www.eia.gov and www.dat.com returned getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND; curl to eia.gov returned 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'. WebSearch is the only working channel and delivered: EIA diesel week ending 10/5 = $6.199 (two secondary sources), DAT PNW reefer -3.2% w/w (week ending 10/3). Could not: primary-verify any number, find EIA week-of-10/12, find national DAT van/reefer/flatbed all-in for weeks ending 10/3 or 10/10, refresh NTI spotAllIn, read the USDA 10/6 FVWTRK PDF (fetchable on s3.amazonaws.com but no extractable text; no PDF tools in sandbox), or source Atlanta->Miami.
